correctness.rationale: The strict model is undirected independent-edge G(n,p), with unordered triples and induced edge counts. At identical triples the indicator covariance is δ_ij q_i−q_i q_j. Only distinct triples sharing two vertices can contribute otherwise. Given the shared edge the two pairs of remaining edges are independent; the conditional mean difference is d_j=q'_j(p)/3 from the Bernoulli binomial mass. Each first triple has 3(n−3) ordered partners of this kind, giving the asserted exact matrix. Off diagonal the sign is that of (n−3)(i−3p)(j−3p)−3p(1−p). Its linear factors after removing positive p or 1−p give the four stated single thresholds; the empty/triangle expression is −3Dp(1−p), and the one-/two-edge polynomial is 3Dp²−3Dp+2(n−3). For n≥4, 1/9<n/(3D)<1, so both roots are interior and straddle 1/3 and 2/3. At n=3, competition on the sole triple makes all mixed covariances negative. The phrase ‘negative dependence’ is supported here only as negative covariance, not a stronger association assertion. Exact independent check: python3 /workspace/reproductions/frozen_checks.py 4 enumerates 8,64,1024 labeled graphs for n=3,4,5, verifies complete matrices at selected rational p, tests rational zeros and signs including both positive tails and the negative center for the (1,2) pair. This bounded check is not a proof of the irrational thresholds or unbounded parameter claims.

evidence: The decisive prior source explicitly assumes n≥4 and independent p∈(0,1), calculates exact covariance of the required ordinary-count basis, and separately displays its limit. Its focus on normal approximation does not diminish the exact equation.

The other inspected induced-count deviation and martingale formulas are related but asymptotic or approximate; Wasserman conditions a directed graph on numbers of choices, and Bhattacharya–Das–Mukherjee sample vertices from a parent graph.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Model-distinct comparators are not used to infer coverage. The exact, not limiting, Bernoulli graph calculation already implies the result on the entire nontrivial domain; n=3 is a multinomial-indicator boundary.

evidence: For total edge, ordinary 2-star and triangle counts T,V,U, respectively, the original census is (C−(n−2)T+V−U, (n−2)T−2V+3U, V−3U, U), where C=binom(n,3). Thus the prior scaled vector ((n−2)T,V,U)/n² gives the entire centered census by multiplying by n² and applying A with rows (−1,1,−1), (1,−2,3), (0,1,−3), (0,0,1).

The exact published matrix is Σ₁=3(n−2)C p(1−p)/n⁴ times vvᵀ+B/(n−2), where v=(1,2p,p²), B has zero first row/column and nonzero block [p(1−p), p²(1−p); p²(1−p), p²(1+p−2p²)/3]. Its congruence n⁴AΣ₁Aᵀ has Av=d, the stated vector of conditional differences. The part other than 3(n−2)C p(1−p) ddᵀ is proportional to C and independent of n. At n=3 the orthogonal-product calculation of §5.1 remains valid, and the direct one-triple limit gives diag(q)−qqᵀ; hence the coefficient of ddᵀ relative to that term is 3(n−3)C p(1−p).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Although ordinary wedges and induced wedges are different statistics, this exact joint 3×3 matrix contains all information for the 4×4 matrix on the deterministic fixed-sum hyperplane. The affine change of basis has no modeling or asymptotic approximation.

The same-date indexed triangle/chordless-cycle threshold is for cycle length at least four, not this census. Ranked hits did not supply a literal six-row table; Eq. (5.1) is an exact finite matrix in equivalent coordinates.

originality.rationale: Reinert–Röllin, arXiv:0912.3425, Eq. (5.1), gives the exact finite-n,p covariance in the same model for a basis of the induced triad census after linear scaling. The invertible affine recoding on the fixed-sum census hyperplane gives the whole frozen matrix. The sign regions are mechanical factorizations of that prior matrix, including the reentrant pair. Independently, indexed record 549b3a6afdfa explicitly gives the (2,3) row and its threshold. The failure is demonstrated implication, not an assertion that all six thresholds were previously printed together.
residual_risks: A literal earlier all-six sign table was not located; the failure does not depend on one.
The portions of Wasserman and the motif sampling source read establish model differences, not comprehensive negative statements about those papers.

value.rationale: The clear sign presentation and conditioning proof are useful exposition, but the entire finite matrix already exists in an equivalent basis and each sign has a routine polynomial check. The most plausible narrowed result, the two-tail (1,2) crossover, is directly forced by the published quadratic after the fixed recoding, as shown above. No nonmechanical precise invariant survives as a justified repair.
